learning_outcomes.text: Acquiring fundamental concepts regarding the physical operation of key non-linear electronic devices (transistors and diodes) and their application in analog electronic circuits.
Using analytical techniques and development methodologies to gain proficiency in the analysis and design of analog electronic circuits.
Ability to design independently based on one's own knowledge and experience, even with incomplete specifications; ability to organize the development stages of an analog circuit.
Ability to present design considerations to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Acquiring the skills necessary to tackle design problems.
Demonstrate knowledge of the basic polarization techniques of a transistor and the genesis of the small signal equivalent models of transistors and diodes.
Demonstrate knowledge of elementary assemblies with their fundamental properties, such as gain and input and output resistances.
Demonstrate knowledge of the main techniques for analyzing the frequency response of an analog circuit.

Demonstrate knowledge of the concept of feedback applied to an electronic amplifier with its effects, advantages and disadvantages on its fundamental properties, such as gain, input and output resistances, band, linearity, phase margin.
Demonstrate knowledge of the analysis techniques of a feedback amplifier as well as of the main compensation techniques.
Be able to read the schematic of a simple amplifier recognizing the elementary assemblies of which it is made up.
Be able to calculate the polarization point of the circuit and deduce the main small signal properties, such as gain, input and output resistances.
Be able to devise and support arguments also relating to properties such as bandwidth, stability and compensation.
Be able to collect and interpret the most relevant aspects of an electronic amplifier, possibly hypothesizing improvement solutions.
Demonstrate that he is able to present the concepts described by the First Descriptor, possibly integrating the presentation with his ideas.
Demonstrate that he is able to concisely explain possible solutions to circuit problems, which may arise during the oral exam.
Be able to undertake subsequent studies with a high degree of autonomy as well as gain knowledge, with the support of advanced books, of some advances themes in their field of study.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to microelectronics and semiconductor physics
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test followed by an oral test; the two parts are inseparable. Admission to the oral test is contingent upon passing the written test. Failure to pass the oral test results in the invalidation of the written test. The final grade is the average of the marks obtained in the two tests and will be announced at the conclusion of the entire examination process. Assessments are graded on a scale of thirty.
